decisions.question: S10 found that the MultiWriterTopic amendment changes type inference: the inferred common type of an event topic and a replay topic moves from Topic<T> to MultiWriterTopic<T>, so `final mixed = [event, replay]; mixed.add(state);` compiles before the amendment and fails after it. Does that make the amendment breaking, so the run stops?

options.label: Compatible; proceed
options.consequence: The amendment stands within v1 with the inference edge recorded in Versioning; topic-codegen@v1 is told to write collection element types out.

options.label: Breaking; stop the run
options.consequence: The owner decides; bus-api@v1 waits, although no code anywhere could be affected.

options.label: Revert to bus-api's ArgumentError fallback
options.consequence: No inference edge, and the StateTopic rule moves from compile time to run time.

decisions.why: The stop condition is an amendment that would break an existing consumer, and no consumer exists: no package, no app, every contract draft. On the merits the edge is of the kind the contract's own Compatible list already accepts (a new top-level name colliding with an import, a new getter shadowing an extension member): it changes no type the Interface states and only bites code that relied on an inferred least upper bound. Keeping compile-time rejection of a publish to a StateTopic is worth more than avoiding an inference change no one depends on. The signal that would change this: any consumer code written against v1 before the amendment.
